description: Learn how to use and configure the ESLint plugin to catch common issues and problems in a Next.js application.
Next.js provides an ESLint configuration package,
, that makes it easy to catch common issues in your application. It includes the
plugin along with recommended rule-sets from
The package provides two main configurations:
: Base configuration with Next.js, React, and React Hooks rules. Supports both JavaScript and TypeScript files.
: Includes everything from the base config, plus upgrades rules that impact
from warnings to errors. Recommended for most projects.
. Use this alongside the base or core-web-vitals config.
Get linting working quickly with the ESLint CLI (flat config):
Install ESLint and the Next.js config:

import { defineConfig, globalIgnores } from 'eslint/config'
import nextVitals from 'eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals'

const eslintConfig = defineConfig([
	...nextVitals,
	// Override default ignores of eslint-config-next.
	globalIgnores([
		// Default ignores of eslint-config-next:
		'.next/**',
		'out/**',
		'build/**',
		'next-env.d.ts',
	]),
])

export default eslintConfig

This approach eliminates the risk of collisions or errors that can occur when the same plugins or parsers are imported across multiple configurations.
If you're adding Next.js to an existing ESLint setup, spread the Next.js config into your array:

, you're adding multiple config objects that include file patterns, plugins, rules, ignores, and parser settings. ESLint applies configs in order, so later rules can override earlier ones for matching files.

This approach works well for straightforward setups. If you have a complex existing config with specific file patterns or plugin configurations that conflict, consider using the plugin directly (as shown above) for more granular control.
